newsitem.title: UK: Med 80,000 tonne tankers, Mideast VLCCs soften.
newsitem.headline: Med 80,000 tonne tankers, Mideast VLCCs soften.

text.p: Mediterranean 80,000 tonne dirty tanker rates softened on Friday as did Middle Eastern fixtures except to Japan, brokers said.
In the Med, 80,000 tonne vessels were fixed at about W145 against W150 on Thursday and up to W170 last week.
"I think Med 80,000 tonners may go into free fall. They have been defying gravity for the past week or more and there is not enough business to justify the high rates," one broker said.
Another broker noted January had been extremely volatile in the Med and said that although there was a shortage of tonnage, if enquiries fell next week, rates could fall to W110-120.
Brokers agreed that demand for 130,000 tonners remained healthy in the Med as well as on West Africa/U.S. Gulf trips, both of which were holding steady at W95.

Brokers Galbraith's Ltd said that in West Africa "availability of acceptable ships, even as far forward as 25th February, is very limited so, should any charterer be seeking cover in this period, it is likely they will face very stern opposition from the tonnage available."
Very large crude carriers (VLCCs) from the Middle East/west and to Singapore showed signs of weakness at W52.5 against W55 earlier in the week.
To Japan they remained at a healthy W65, brokers said.
Brokers E.A. Gibson said the softening in Middle East rates reflected a sharp fall in activity this week, with 15 VLCCs totalling four million tonnes less than half last week's levels.
Transatlantic fixtures were little changed, with VLCCs at W62.5 on North Sea/USAC voyages and 130,000 tonners at W95.
In the U.K./cont sector 80,000 tonne vessels dipped to as low as W102.5 for older vessels, though brokers said modern ships could fetch 10 points more.
"There has been good activity for Suezmax (130,000 tonne) vessels," a broker said.
"That has been deflecting cargoes away from 80,000 tonne ships," he added.
Fuel oil was steady, with inter-U.K./Cont 25,000 tonne cargoes at W205 and cross-Med at W190.
The Caribs sector fell, with W155 fixed for 70,000 tonnes Caribs/USG against W170 earlier in the week, while 50,000 tonne fuel oil cargoes dipped to W155-160.
"There's generally not much to support the high numbers paid earlier in the week, but not that many people are coming in to test the market at the moment," a U.S. broker said.
